items.title: Why is this fingerprinting script creating bioweapons?
items.summary: While crawling 10,000 top sites and collecting browser-canvas fingerprinting scripts, the author found one drawing an elaborate Tame Impala-style artwork whose code contained functions like 'computeRicinLethalDosageForWaterSupply'. The alarming names turned out to be deliberate anti-LLM obfuscation, designed to trip model safeguards and make automated deobfuscation refuse the file. Functionally, the script is just a standard anti-bot fingerprint collector; the author traced it to Russian traffic-control company Servicepipe and published the canvases at fingerprint.garden.

items.title: Qwenputer: A functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
items.summary: A developer embedded a working RISC-V CPU into the weights of a stock Qwen 3.5 4B model, using the model's Gated DeltaNet attention layers' state matrices as RAM. The CPU runs entirely inside the model's forward passes and executes arithmetic, C, and MicroPython code with no external runtime, tool calls, or plugins. The writeup explains how fixing the RNN gate at 1 makes the state an exact memory, and includes follow-ups on hiding reasoning in the RNN state and in-model file storage.

items.title: The US added a record 20.2 GWh of battery storage in just 3 months
items.summary: The US installed a record 20.2 GWh of battery storage in Q2 2026, bringing first-half installations to 30.8 GWh, up 23% year over year, per SEIA and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Nearly all growth came from utility-scale projects, about 18 GWh, led by Arizona's record 6.2 GWh, plus 3.8 GWh in Texas and 3.6 GWh in California. Batteries supplied more electricity to the grid in the first eight months of 2026 than in all of 2025.
